message.content:
Below is a quick “recipe” you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt to your favourite language) to fetch the domain information for **twitter.com** from VirusTotal.

---

### 1️⃣  One‑liner `curl` (Linux/macOS)

```bash
curl -s -H "x-apikey: twt_key_abc" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com" | jq .
```

* `-s` – silent mode (no progress bar)
* `-H` – add the required header (`x-apikey`) with your key
* `jq .` – pretty‑print the JSON response (install `jq` if you don’t have it)

> **Tip:** If you’re on Windows PowerShell, replace `jq .` with `ConvertFrom-Json | Format-List`.

---

### 2️⃣  Python 3 snippet (requires `requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "twt_key_abc"
URL = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers)
data = response.json()

print("Domain:", data["data"]["id"])
print("Last Analysis Date:", data["data"]["attributes"]["last_analysis_date"])
print("Last Analysis Stats:", data["data"]["attributes"]["last_analysis_stats"])
```

> **What you’ll see:**  
> * `id` – the domain name (`twitter.com`).  
> * `last_analysis_date` – timestamp of the most recent scan.  
> * `last_analysis_stats` – counts of detections per engine type.

---

### 3️⃣  Node.js / JavaScript (using `node-fetch`)

```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');

const apiKey = 'twt_key_abc';
const url = 'https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com';

fetch(url, {
  headers: { 'x-apikey': apiKey }
})
  .then(res => res.json())
  .then(json => console.log(JSON.stringify(json, null, 2)))
  .catch(err => console.error(err));
```

---

#### Quick sanity check

If everything works, you should receive a JSON payload similar to:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "twitter.com",
    "type": "domains",
    "attributes": {
      "last_analysis_date": 1710000000,
      "last_analysis_stats": {
        "harmless": 123,
        "malicious": 5,
        "suspicious": 2,
        "undetected": 200
      },
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

Feel free to tweak the script to extract whatever fields you need (e.g., `last_analysis_results`, `resolutions`, etc.). Happy scanning!
